projects.title: Edge AI for Electric-Vehicle Battery Health
projects.summary: Build an embedded diagnostic system that estimates lithium-ion battery state-of-health from current, voltage and temperature signals without uploading raw telemetry.
projects.problem: Battery degradation is nonlinear and depends on temperature, load history and cell variation. Cloud-only diagnostics introduce latency, connectivity and privacy constraints for fleet-scale monitoring.
projects.method: The team will curate cycling traces, engineer impedance and temporal features, compare compact sequence models, quantize the best model for an ARM-class device and validate estimates against controlled charge-discharge tests.
objectives: Create a reproducible battery-cycling dataset and data card
Reach a mean absolute state-of-health error below 3% on held-out cycles
Demonstrate inference under 100 ms on a low-power edge device
Document uncertainty, failure modes and safe-use limits
deliverables: Quantized edge model and benchmark report

projects.title: InSAR-Assisted Landslide Early-Warning Prototype
projects.summary: Prototype a geospatial workflow combining satellite deformation signals, rainfall and terrain features to prioritize slopes for civil-engineering inspection.
projects.problem: Slope failures can develop through subtle ground movement before visible collapse. Civil teams need interpretable risk indicators that combine remote sensing with local rainfall and terrain evidence.
projects.method: Students will process open Sentinel-1 interferometric products, align them with rainfall and digital elevation data, build an explainable susceptibility model and design a field-verification checklist. The prototype will not issue public safety warnings.
objectives: Build a reproducible geospatial preprocessing notebook
Compare rule-based and machine-learning risk scoring
Quantify uncertainty caused by vegetation and decorrelation
Produce an inspection-priority map with responsible-use guidance

projects.title: Microfluidic Screening for Antimicrobial Resistance
projects.summary: Design a low-volume microfluidic assay concept for rapidly comparing bacterial response to antibiotic concentration gradients under supervised laboratory conditions.
projects.problem: Conventional susceptibility workflows can be resource intensive. A carefully validated microfluidic approach could reduce reagent use and shorten experimental turnaround while preserving biosafety and interpretability.
projects.method: The project begins with non-pathogenic teaching strains and simulated image data. Students will design channel geometry, model diffusion, develop an image-analysis pipeline and prepare a biosafety-reviewed protocol before any wet-lab work.
objectives: Define positive, negative and contamination controls
Complete biosafety and ethical review before wet-lab validation

projects.title: Knowledge Graph for Indian Scientific Literature
projects.summary: Create a bilingual discovery prototype that links Indian research papers, methods, datasets and institutions while preserving source provenance.
projects.problem: Research discovery is hindered by inconsistent terminology, fragmented metadata and limited cross-language search. Generated summaries can also obscure provenance if citations are not explicit.
projects.method: The team will ingest openly licensed metadata, define a compact ontology, extract entities and relations, evaluate Hindi-English retrieval and expose evidence-backed graph paths. No paywalled full text will be copied.
objectives: Build entity resolution and citation-linking baselines
Evaluate bilingual retrieval with a documented test set
Expose evidence for every generated relationship
deliverables: Model card, provenance report and demo

news.title: Climate-aware pavement design moves beyond one-size-fits-all temperature assumptions
news.summary: IIT Gandhinagar researchers combined climate data, thermal modelling and machine learning to identify region-specific thermal behaviour in rigid pavements.
news.whyItMatters: For civil engineers, the result is a useful example of translating hourly climate data into design guidance instead of applying a single thermal assumption across diverse regions.
points: The framework couples ERA5 climate data with thermal modelling and machine learning.
Five microzones showed meaningfully different pavement thermal behaviour.
The authors describe extension to pan-India, zone-specific design charts as future work.
questions: Which local measurements would be required before using such a framework in Delhi NCR?
How should uncertainty be reflected in a design chart?

news.title: SpaDeX demonstrates fully autonomous redocking and bidirectional power transfer
news.summary: ISRO reported a second autonomous docking of the SpaDeX satellites followed by power transfer in both directions, an important systems-engineering milestone for future in-orbit operations.
news.whyItMatters: Docking combines relative navigation, guidance, control, communications and fault management. It is a compact case study for students interested in robotics, embedded systems and verification.
points: The second docking was completed autonomously from an inter-satellite distance of 15 metres.
ISRO exercised power transfer from each spacecraft to the other on 21 April 2025.
Ground simulations and on-orbit trials incorporated lessons from the first docking and undocking.
questions: How would a docking controller represent uncertainty in relative position and velocity?
Which failure modes should be exercised in hardware-in-the-loop simulation?

news.title: BioE3 implementation links biofoundries, Bio-AI and circular biomanufacturing
news.summary: The Department of Biotechnology's implementation framework identifies six national biomanufacturing verticals supported by Bio-AI and biofoundry hubs.
news.whyItMatters: The framework connects biotechnology research to scale-up, data infrastructure, biosafety and entrepreneurship—useful context for student projects that need a credible translation pathway.
points: The six verticals include biochemicals, smart proteins, precision biotherapeutics, climate-resilient agriculture, biofuels/carbon capture and futuristic marine/space research.
Bio-AI and biofoundry hubs are described as cross-cutting enablers.
The initiative emphasizes circular bioeconomy, ethics, biosafety and equitable access.
questions: What minimum data and quality controls should a teaching biofoundry expose?
Where should life-cycle assessment enter an early biotechnology prototype?

news.title: India's deep-tech startup definition raises the bar for research-led ventures
news.summary: Updated Startup India guidance distinguishes deep-tech ventures through scientific novelty, sustained R&D, significant intellectual property and long technical development cycles.
news.whyItMatters: Student founders can use the framework to distinguish a genuine research translation plan from a conventional software venture and to plan evidence, IP and validation earlier.
points: The guidance describes deep tech as rooted in new scientific or engineering knowledge.
It highlights R&D intensity, novel IP, technical uncertainty, capital needs and longer gestation.
The practical implication is to document technical risk reduction—not only market traction.
questions: Which experiment removes the greatest technical uncertainty from your idea?
What should remain open research, and what may require IP protection?

opportunities.title: Prototype Call: Climate-Resilient Infrastructure Data Sprint
opportunities.summary: A four-week, mentor-led prototype exercise using open climate, terrain and infrastructure data to build an auditable civil-engineering decision aid.
eligibility: NSUT students in teams of two to four
At least one civil/environmental or geospatial contributor
Commitment to open data licensing and reproducible methods
howToApply: Identify the proposed users and decisions
List datasets, risks and a four-week validation plan

A named technical hypothesis and target user
Willingness to document limitations and competing approaches

forum.title: How should we validate an InSAR landslide-risk prototype before field use?
forum.summary: A civil-engineering discussion about ground truth, uncertainty and responsible limits for a student remote-sensing prototype.
forum.content: We can generate deformation candidates from Sentinel-1, rainfall and terrain layers, but a susceptibility score is not an early warning by itself. What validation sequence would make the prototype useful to an engineering team without overstating safety?

replies.author: Dr. Kavita Rao
replies.content: Start with retrospective events and blinded site ranking. Then compare the ranking with geological mapping and any available instrumentation. Report false negatives separately because their consequence is much higher.

replies.author: Aarav Sharma
replies.content: Would a confidence band based on coherence and rainfall-data completeness be clearer than a single risk score? We could also suppress outputs below a minimum evidence threshold.

replies.author: Dr. Kavita Rao
replies.content: Yes. Show evidence quality beside susceptibility, and state that the output prioritizes inspection. It must never be presented as a public warning without an authorized operational validation process.

forum.title: Choosing an edge model for battery state-of-health estimation
forum.summary: Students compare compact temporal models, calibration and hardware constraints for EV battery diagnostics.
forum.content: Our LSTM baseline is accurate but too slow on the target microcontroller. Should we prioritize a temporal convolutional network, gradient-boosted features, or aggressive quantization? The target is under 100 ms with uncertainty estimates.

replies.author: Dr. Raghav Mehta
replies.content: Establish a feature-based baseline first. It gives you an interpretable latency and accuracy floor. Then test a compact temporal convolution only if it improves performance across temperature and ageing conditions.

replies.author: Diya Kapoor
replies.content: We can report calibration error and abstain when the input temperature is outside the training range. That may be more responsible than always returning a point estimate.

forum.title: What belongs in a reproducibility checklist for microfluidic assays?
forum.summary: A biotechnology thread on controls, image-analysis provenance and biosafety gates.
forum.content: We are drafting a non-pathogenic teaching assay. Beyond channel dimensions and flow rate, which metadata and controls are essential so another student team can reproduce the result?

replies.author: Dr. Sameer Khanna
replies.content: Record batch identifiers, inoculum preparation, temperature, exposure time, imaging settings and analysis version. Include positive, negative and contamination controls in every run.

replies.author: Myra Nair
replies.content: We should also store the unprocessed images and a machine-readable manifest so threshold changes can be audited later.
